title: hello-cli — the minimal vertical slice (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Smallest possible slice: a spec in, a streaming chat agent out.”
beats.script: Smallest possible slice: a spec in, a streaming chat agent out. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens README.md now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env for the run beats. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and which runtime spine to compile.”
beats.script: Two lines: what it's called, and which runtime spine to compile. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 1 through 2 of crewhaus.yaml, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: “A model and instructions — that's the whole agent.”
beats.script: A model and instructions — that's the whole agent. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 3 through 7 of crewhaus.yaml become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”
beats.script: Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.”
beats.script: The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints the IR for target cli.

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN.”
beats.script: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “One generated TypeScript file, imports and all — you own the output, not a framework.”
beats.script: One generated TypeScript file, imports and all — you own the output, not a framework. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash agent.ts now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.

beats.label: Launch the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “crewhaus run compiles in memory and drops into a streaming chat loop.”
beats.script: Crewhaus run compiles in memory and drops into a streaming chat loop. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. Interactive REPL; needs Anthropic credentials.

beats.label: Ask it something
beats.cue: [needs-key] Two sentences or fewer — the instructions hold.
beats.script: Two sentences or fewer — the instructions hold. [[pause:1.2s]] The driver sends the next user turn into the active session: “In one sentence: what is a meta-harness?” The resulting answer is the live evidence for the contract described in the first chunk.
beats.text: In one sentence: what is a meta-harness?

beats.label: Ask for more detail
beats.cue: [needs-key] “…unless the user asks for more detail.” — it obeys the escape hatch.
beats.script: “…unless the user asks for more detail.” — it obeys the escape hatch. [[pause:1.2s]] The driver sends the next user turn into the active session: “Now give me more detail, in four sentences.” Watch the response demonstrate the behavior while preserving the same session context.
beats.text: Now give me more detail, in four sentences.

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.script: “exit” returns to the shell. [[pause:1.2s]] The driver sends exit to close the active REPL cleanly. The terminal returns to a normal shell while the generated artifacts and session history remain available.

groups.title: One more thing · the bundle is yours

beats.cue: “Six pinned @crewhaus deps — and --check already resolved them into a bun.lock beside it. That's what makes the bundle yours.”
beats.script: Six pinned @crewhaus deps — and --check already resolved them into a bun.lock beside it. That's what makes the bundle yours. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash package.json now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.
